newsitem.title: UK: Currency, lack of sellers subdue UK grain markets.
newsitem.headline: Currency, lack of sellers subdue UK grain markets.

text.p: A strong sterling against other European currencies and a lack of sellers subdued trading on the UK LIFFE grains futures and the cash markets.
"The market is at contract lows and no one has the courage to sell it any lower," said on broker.
"The market has a long way to go yet but people wont sell it short because the farmers are still hanging on to their material," said another.
In cash market trading delivered milling wheat and feed wheat was trading around one stg down while buyers and sellers on the fob market were one stg lower and about as far apart.
Feed wheat in East Anglia was fetching 86 stg for June and 87.50 stg for harvest material.
LIFFE wheat futures market lost 0.75 to 0.65 stg on the day while barley was 0.25 stg lower.
Turnovers were light at 322 lots for feed wheat and 16 lots for feed barley.
New crop November was the most active position in feed wheat with 257 lots against it and a last trade of 90.15 stg, 0.70 stg down.
